details.publicNotes:
While the world might often seem unpredictable and chaotic, cosiadifexes understand that very few things are truly random; instead, they simply arise from a greater complex order impossible for mortal minds to fully comprehend. Cosiadifexes represent this same duality between the perceived randomness of events and the complex chains of processes that allow them to occur. Using only advanced mathematical reasoning through their exceptional intelligence, a cosiadifex is able to perfectly predict the cascading consequences of any given action and, given enough time, they can even trace the link between any two events across space and time. They can also extrapolate past circumstances from present conditions, allowing them to investigate a scene and deduce much of what happened there.

Aeons are caretakers of order and balance, who watch over reality and guard it from the excesses that would throw it astray. Those who seek to cause discord and chaos will find themselves at odds with aeons' goals.

Clean Results

For true predictability, a cosiadifex prefers a system that doesn't contain mortals, whose otherwise deterministic biological processes are messed up by that pesky free will of theirs. In order to preserve a critical chain of events from tampering, a cosiadifex is not above forcefully eliminating anyone who happens to blunder by.

description.value: 100 feet. A fractrix can communicate mentally with any creatures in the aura using wordless psychic projections. They don't need to share a language, though the aeon's meaning to non-aeons can be vague and is often mysterious. An aeon can use this ability to communicate flawlessly with any other aeon on the same plane as themselves.

Because the cosiadifex relies so strongly on their ability to connect cause and effect and understand the true nature of causality, the rare instances of true randomness in the universe are capable of confounding them and throwing them off their stride. Whenever the cosiadifex witnesses a random activity or effect, such as the actions of a @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} creature, the effects of a protean's warpwave, or a wild magic effect from a wellspring dragon, they are @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round.

You gain a sixth sense that warns you of danger that might befall the target of the spell. If you choose a creature other than yourself as the target, you create a psychic link through which you can inform the target of danger. This link is a mental effect. Due to the amount of information this spell requires you to process, you can't have more than one foresight spell in effect at a time. Casting foresight again ends the previous foresight. While foresight is in effect, the target gains a +2 status bonus to initiative rolls and isn't @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} against @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.VRSef5y1LmL2Hkjf]{Undetected} creatures or when flanked. In addition, you gain the following reaction: @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.actions.Item.VOEWhPQfN3lvHivK]{Foresight}

You manifest a bubble of distorted time. The bubble is filled with tiny pockets where time runs slightly faster or slightly slower than normal. Movement through these temporal pockets is dangerous and disorienting, as muscles and bones slide out of sync with each other. Creatures that enter or begin their turn in the area must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 2} until it leaves the spell's area.

Failure The creature is clumsy 2 until it leaves the spell's area. While it remains in the area, whenever it uses a move or manipulate action, it takes 6d8 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} until it leaves the spell's area.

Heightened (+1) The damage for using move or manipulate actions increases by 1d8.

You conjure a spectral scythe that gradually phases into reality above a target's head and follows them wherever they go. At the end of the creature's next three turns, an ominous bell tolls, and the creature must succeed at a Will save or be @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure); this effect has the emotion, fear, and mental traits. After the third toll, the scythe swings, striking the creature in the neck and dealing 10d10 slashing damage with a basic Fortitude save. If the spell reduces a target to 0 Hit Points, they die; this is a death effect.

Heightened (+1) Increase the damage by 2d10.

Opening your mind to mental echoes, you gain impressions from past events that occurred in your current location. Retrocognition reveals psychic impressions from events that occurred over the course of the last day throughout the first minute of the duration, followed by impressions from the next day back the next minute, and so on. These echoes don't play out like a vision but instead reveal impressions of emotions and metaphors that provide cryptic clues and details of the past. If you witness a traumatic or turbulent event through an impression, the spell ends unless you succeed at a Will save with a DC of at least 30 and possibly as much as 50, depending on the severity of the event. The GM determines whether an event is traumatic and chooses the DC.

Heightened (8th) You gain impressions of events that occurred over the previous year for each minute you concentrate, instead of the previous day, though the details diminish, making it harder to distinguish impressions from all but the most major events.

Heightened (9th) You gain impressions of events that occurred over the previous century for each minute you concentrate, instead of the previous day, though the details diminish, making it almost impossible to distinguish impressions from all but the most major events.

Requirements You have a planar key for the destination plane, used as a locus

You and your allies traverse the barriers between planes of existence. The targets move to another plane, such as the Plane of Fire, the Netherworld, or the Outer Rifts. You must know the destination plane exists and use a magic planar key created from material from that plane as a locus for the spell. While the planar keys for most prominent planes are uncommon, just like the spell interplanar teleport, more obscure planes and demiplanes often have rare or possibly even unique planar keys.

The spell is highly imprecise, and you appear 1d20×25 miles from the last place one of the targets (of your choice) was located the last time that target traveled to the plane. If it's the first time traveling to a particular plane for all targets, you appear at a random location on the plane. Interplanar teleport doesn't provide a means of return travel, though casting interplanar teleport again allows you to return to your previous plane unless there are extenuating circumstances.

You delve into the possible futures of the next few seconds to understand all the ways your foe might avoid harm, then cast out a vision of that future to those around you. Designate a creature. The first time each target makes an attack roll against that creature during true target's duration, the attacker rolls twice and uses the better result. The attacker also ignores circumstance penalties to the attack roll and any flat check required due to the designated creature being @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} or @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden}.

You conjure up a wall of slowed time, which is both transparent and sepia-colored. The wall is 1 inch thick, up to 120 feet long, and up to 20 feet high. You can shape the wall's path, placing each 5 feet of the wall on the border between squares. The wall doesn't need to stand vertically or be supported by any surface. You must conjure the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost.

Mindless creatures, unattended objects (including thrown weapons and ammunition), and spell effects that pass through the wall are trapped within, emerging 1 round after they enter it. Held objects that enter the wall, such as a melee weapon used to Strike a creature on the other side of the wall, become stuck for 1 round as well. The creature can choose to drop the held object; if they do, the object continues its trajectory after it is freed from the wall's effect; this would allow a melee weapon to resolve the Strike before falling to the ground. However, attacks and targeted effects whose targets have moved from their original position since they entered the wall automatically miss.

Non-mindless creatures that enter the wall of time lose one action from their current turn if they can; if they can't, either because they are on their final action for the turn or it is not their turn, they are instead @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}.

You peek into the future. Choose a particular goal or activity you plan to engage in within 1 week, or an event you expect might happen within 1 week. You learn a cryptic clue or piece of advice that could help with the chosen event, often in the form of a rhyme or omen.

You pull an echo of your target's recent injuries through time, inflicting them anew. Choose a type of damage that the target has taken since the beginning of your last turn. The target takes 2d6 damage of that type.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

description.value: You see things within 60 feet as they actually are. The GM rolls a secret counteract check against any illusion, morph or polymorph effect in the area, but only for the purpose of determining whether you see through it (for instance, if the check succeeds against a polymorph spell, you can see the creature's true form, but you don't end the polymorph spell).

The cosiadifex makes a shard Strike, attempting to trigger an improbable set of circumstances that brings disaster to their enemies. If the Strike hits, the cosiadifex can make another Strike at a different target within 30 feet of the target they just hit, repeating this process until they miss a Strike. The cosiadifex can't target the same creature twice with this ability. The damage type of any Strikes after the first depends on the nature of the chain reaction caused, such as dealing fire damage by causing an oil lantern to explode. Any fortune effects that apply to the first Strike apply to every Strike in the chain.

Frequency once per hour

Effect The cosiadifex's mantle ripples slightly, disturbing the air in an impossibly precise fashion that stirs up a tornado that appears at the beginning of the cosiadifex's next turn. The tornado has a @Template[burst|distance:15]{15-foot radius} and is up to 100 feet tall. The wind imposes a –4 circumstance penalty to physical ranged attacks, and the air in the area is greater difficult terrain for flying creatures. Creatures that enter or begin their turn within the tornado take @Damage[10d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:38|basic] save). Creatures that fail the save are also thrown 20 feet upward (or 40 feet on a critical failure). A creature can only take damage or be thrown by Ominous Wingbeat once per round. The cosiadifex can Sustain the tornado to extend the effect for up to 1 minute; when they do, they can also move the tornado up to 50 feet in any direction.
